tables.name: companies
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE companies (
            cik TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            entity_type TEXT,
            sic TEXT,
            sic_description TEXT,

tables.name: filings

            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            cik TEXT NOT NULL,
            accession_number TEXT NOT NULL,

tables.name: financial_facts
tables.sql:
CREATE TABLE financial_facts (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                cik TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_value REAL,
                unit TEXT NOT NULL,
                fact_category TEXT NOT NULL,
                fiscal_year INTEGER,
                fiscal_period TEXT,
                end_date DATE,
                accession_number TEXT,
                form_type TEXT,
                filed_date DATE,
                frame TEXT,
                dimension_segment TEXT,
                dimension_geography TEXT,
                created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
                FOREIGN KEY (cik) REFERENCES companies(cik)
            )

message.content:
I have sufficient evidence. The most recent period in the database is Q2 2025 (ended 2025-06-30), and I can compare it to the FY2024 year-end (2024-12-31).

**Answer: Overall, ServiceNow's liquidity and asset base strengthened in the most recent period (Q2 2025, ended 2025-06-30, 10-Q accession 0001373715-25-000276), compared with FY2024 year-end (2024-12-31, 10-K accession 0001373715-25-000010).**

Key figures (USD, consolidated, no segment dimension):

| Metric | 2024-12-31 (FY2024) | 2025-06-30 (Q2 2025) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total assets | $20.383B (fact 1335160) | $22.051B (fact 1335164) | +8.2% |
| Current assets | $9.187B (fact 1335266) | $9.275B (fact 1335270) | +1.0% |
| Cash & cash equivalents | $2.304B (fact 1336646) | $3.124B (fact 1336650) | +35.6% |
| Current liabilities | $8.358B (fact 1344287) | $8.495B (fact 1344291) | +1.6% |
| Stockholders' equity | $9.609B (fact 1351551) | $10.932B (fact 1351556) | +13.8% |
| Current ratio (derived) | 1.10x | 1.09x | roughly flat |

Interpretation:
- **Asset base strengthened:** total assets rose ~8.2% and stockholders' equity rose ~13.8% over the six months, indicating a larger and better-capitalized balance sheet.
- **Liquidity improved on the cash side:** cash and cash equivalents grew ~35.6% (from $2.30B to $3.12B), a clear strengthening of the most liquid resource.
- **Working-capital cushion was essentially unchanged:** current assets grew only ~1.0% while current liabilities grew ~1.6%, so the derived current ratio slipped marginally from ~1.10x to ~1.09x — still comfortably above 1.0x but not an improvement.
- The FY2024 10-K's Liquidity and Capital Resources discussion states management expects "cash flows generated from operations, cash, cash equivalents and investments will be sufficient to meet our liquidity needs for at least the next 12 months" (chunk 1373715/now-20241231:200215) — a forward-looking management assessment, not a realized result.

Limitations: The current ratio is a derived calculation (current assets ÷ current liabilities), not a directly disclosed field. The most recent period available is Q2 2025 (a point-in-time balance sheet), so this compares a mid-year snapshot to the prior fiscal year-end rather than two full-year periods. The bundled local annual report is FY2024 only; the Q2 2025 figures come from the structured XBRL facts (10-Q accession 0001373715-25-000276), not from a bundled report text.
